channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Iran’s IRGC claims attack on Togolese oil tanker for 'illegal transit' in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Thursday that a Togo-flagged oil ‌tanker was struck ‌while attempting to make an “illegal passage” through the Strait of ‌Hormuz, Arab news reported.

item.title: RBA's Bullock: At August board meeting, risks to outlook were skewed to the upside
item.description: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Michele Bullock said on Friday that risks to outlook were skewed to the upside at August board meeting.

item.title: 1.9%: Japan’s National CPI steadies in August
item.description: Japan’s National Consumer Price Index (CPI) climbed by 1.9% YoY in August, compared to the previous reading of 1.9%, according to the latest data released by the Japan Statistics Bureau on Friday.

item.title: Bank of Japan is set to raise interest rates as inflation, economic growth support tighter policy
item.description: The Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) monetary policy meeting will close a week packed with central bank decisions on Friday, with markets particularly interested in confirming expectations of a hawkish shift that has boosted a strong Japanese Yen (JPY) recovery in September.

item.title: Gold rebounds to near $4,350 on weaker US Dollar, falling oil prices
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) rises to near $4,345 during the early Asian session on Friday. The precious metal rebounds from a six-week low amid falling oil prices and a weaker US Dollar (USD). Traders continue to assess the latest Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike and policy cues.

item.title: Australian Dollar finds a floor as Oil retreat loosens USD’s grip
item.description: The Australian Dollar recovered some ground versus the US Dollar on Thursday, following the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy decision on Wednesday, which witnessed a 0.25% rate hike and paved the way for further tightening.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Spinning tops warn bulls near 180.00
item.description: The EUR/JPY drops by about 0.08% on Thursday, forming back-to-back spinning tops near the 180.00 area, the top of a consolidation range capped to the downside by 178.00. At the time of writing, the cross-pair trades at 179.02, below its opening price.

item.title: US Dollar slips against the Japanese Yen before the Bank of Japan raises rates
item.description: USD/JPY trades near 156.00 after a session high at 156.32 and a low at 155.34, which leaves it three Yen above the September 8 low and four below the September 2 high. The Bank of Japan announces at 02:45 GMT on Friday and a quarter-point increase to 1.25% is priced at 100%.

item.title: British Pound slides after the Bank of England stays put
item.description: GBP/USD trades near 1.3350 on Thursday after a session low at 1.3336, its weakest since the end of July, and it has been under its 200-day average since Wednesday.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Evening star puts 207.00 back in play
item.description: GBP/JPY makes a U-turn and loses about 0.39% on Thursday as risk appetite improves, while traders await a potential rate hike by the Bank of Japan (BoJ) later in Friday’s session. The cross-pair trades at 208.32 after reaching a high of 209.19.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Strong Dollar keeps pair supported – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategist Christopher Wong highlights that Singapore Dollar (SGD) remains largely driven by the broader Dollar story after the FOMC, given its high sensitivity to USD moves.

item.title: Thai Baht: Electronics boom offers limited FX support – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan remains cautious on the Thai Baht, keeping the USD/THB forecast at 34.00 by year-end.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar eases ahead of Bank of Japan decision
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) is ending Thursday softer. The US Dollar Index (DXY) hovers just above the 100.00 mark after climbing to a seven-week high earlier in the week. The sideways action follows Wednesday's decision by the Federal Reserve (Fed) to raise interest rates for the first time since 2023.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Bulls threaten bearish setup after Fed hike
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) surges to five-day highs above $66.00 on Thursday as traders digest the Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike on Wednesday. Meanwhile, a drop in US Treasury yields is undermining the Greenback, which clings to early gains but has barely changed.

item.title: Gold shrugs off Fed hike as falling yields reopen path to $4,400
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) rallies on Thursday, up by more than 2% as investors digest the latest rate hike by the Federal Reserve (Fed), while a fall in Oil prices pushed the US Dollar and US yields lower.

item.title: Australian and New Zealand Dollars dig in ahead of a Japanese rate hike
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) trades near 111.00 against the Japanese Yen (JPY) and the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) near 89.50 on Thursday, both a little higher and both a long way below where they were in August.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: PBoC accepts slower credit as summit nears – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s China-focused FX Research highlights that PBoC Governor Pan Gongsheng framed weaker loan growth as part of structural upgrading, signalling no imminent credit-driven stimulus.

item.title: Crude Oil sells off and takes it all back on Saudi cargoes through Oman
item.description: Crude Oil trades near $97.50, which is where it opened on Thursday, after a drop to $94.50 and a full recovery. Saudi Arabia is offering Asian refiners extra cargoes handed over outside the Strait of Hormuz, and the price treated that as more oil.

item.title: Euro climbs as Sterling slips on cautious BoE hold
item.description: EUR/GBP is trading higher on Thursday, climbing toward the 0.8600 barrier and touching its highest in several days. The Pound has slipped across the board after the Bank of England (BoE) held interest rates and struck a more cautious tone than much of the market had priced in.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Bearish bias against US Dollar - UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/SGD surged to 1.2784 and closed at 1.2783, its largest one-day gain in three months, with strong momentum despite overbought conditions.

item.title: Brazilian Real: 200-DMA capping losses against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s technical team notes USD/BRL’s decline stalled near 4.88 in May and the pair has since traded within a base. Price action struggles above the 200-day moving average, signalling weak upside momentum.

item.title: Japanese Yen awaits fresh direction from Bank of Japan interest rate decision
item.description: USD/JPY trades cautiously on Thursday as attention shifts to the Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) monetary policy decision on Friday after the Federal Reserve (Fed) delivered a widely expected 25-basis-point rate hike on Wednesday.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Higher-for-longer path reshapes cuts – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior Macro Strategist Bas van Geffen discusses the latest FOMC decision, noting a unanimous 25 bps hike in the Federal funds rate and a shift to a higher policy rate trajectory for similar inflation outcomes.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: RSI nears overbought territory
item.description: USD/CHF trades slightly lower on Thursday as the Swiss Franc (CHF) regains some ground after falling for six straight days.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average rebounds as Crude Oil and bond yields fall
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) trades above 51,800 on Thursday, back over the 51,500 area it sold through on Wednesday, when the Federal Reserve (Fed) raised its rate for the first time in three years and the index fell to its lowest level in three months.

item.title: Gold climbs over 2% as US Dollar trims post-Fed gains
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) holds near its daily high on Thursday after rebounding sharply earlier in the day as the US Dollar trims some of its post-Fed gains. A cooldown in the Oil rally also pulls US Treasury yields away from their recent highs, lending additional support to the precious metal.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar gains ground as GDP growth beats expectations
item.description: NZD/USD rebounds on Thursday, trading around 0.5730 at the time of writing, up 0.35% on the day. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) benefits from stronger-than-expected domestic growth data, allowing the pair to recover from the two-month low reached on Wednesday.

item.title: British Pound loses its footing as BoE hold meets Fed hike
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) extends its losses on Thursday after the Bank of England's (BoE) decision to hold rates unchanged in a 6-3 vote, while leaving the door open for a potential hike.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Further weakness could target 157.30 against US Dollar - UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/JPY surged above 156.30 to a high of 156.41, with momentum still modest but supportive of further gains. Intraday, the pair could test 156.50 while holding above support at 155.40.

item.title: Euro: Stabilizing with policy support – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret say EUR/USD is stabilizing after Wednesday’s Fed decision, as improving Germany-US 2-year yield spreads and a hawkish ECB stance support the euro.
